title: Property
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze the acquisition of property, possession and adverse possession, estates and future interests, concurrent ownership, landlord and tenant, real estate transactions and recording acts, mortgages, easements and covenants, zoning and takings.

weeks.4: Future interests and the Rule Against Perpetuities

blocks.deliverable: Analyze an adverse possession claim element by element.
Name the estates and interests created by ten conveyances.
Explain what happens to a joint tenancy when one tenant conveys.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a constructive-eviction claim.
Apply race, notice and race-notice statutes to a chain of title.
Decide whether a covenant runs with the land and whether a regulation is a taking.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Title and land-use memo: from a supplied chain of title and a proposed development, write a 2,000-word memo on ownership, recording, easement, covenant and zoning issues.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
